item.title: Unit tests mark territory more than squash bugs
item.description: I am a programmer who has worked a lot on hardware, and from that point of view, software testing looks horrible, since software is full of bugs. And you can explain this with, well, they push programmers to ship buggy code since you can always fix the bugs later, and so the program is always full of bugs to be fixed later — whereas with hardware, bugs are often (not always!) catastrophic, so they have no choice but to let you fix them, even if it takes some time.

item.title: The Half-Life of an Instruction
item.description: Two French examples. That is all it took. I told DeepSeek’s larger model, V4 Pro, to translate every question into Russian. One earlier turn in which the assistant had answered in French was enough to make it slip 17 times in 100. Two, and it answered in French 90 times out of 90. Switch on thinking mode - the setting where the model writes out its reasoning before it answers - and the same model followed the instruction between 89 and 100 times in 100 at every number of turns I tested, up to 50.
